No. 1 Miami visits Chapel Hill after Malachi Toney's record-setting performance against Pittsburgh; ABC prime-time ACC matchup.

setup: No. 1 Miami travels to Chapel Hill at 7:30 p.m. Eastern on ABC carrying a 7–0 record and the nation's most prolific offense at 49.0 points and 551.9 yards per game. Quarterback Darian Mensah and receiver Malachi Toney just fueled a 52–23 win over Pitt; North Carolina (4–3) has battled through a more uneven season and must find ways to keep the Hurricanes from turning this into a track meet.

things.title: MIAMI'S PASSING GAME VS. UNC'S COVERAGE
things.body: Miami averages 340.7 passing yards per game, while Toney caught 16 passes for 194 yards and three scores against Pittsburgh. UNC must tackle immediately after the catch and keep Mensah from finding one-on-one shots downfield; asking its secondary to survive a steady diet of isolated matchups is dangerous.

things.title: NORTH CAROLINA MUST STAY ON THE FIELD
things.body: Miami converts 54.5% of its third downs, among the best marks nationally; North Carolina's defense allows a 43.1% conversion rate. The Tar Heels need to reverse that trend, avoid quick three-and-outs from Billy Edwards Jr.'s offense and shorten the game enough to reduce Miami's possessions.

things.title: THE GROUND GAME SETS THE TERMS
things.body: Miami averages 211.1 rushing yards per game and holds opponents to only 60.0, the nation's stingiest rushing allowance. North Carolina has managed just 114.0 on the ground, so staying balanced without wasting early downs is a tall order. Negative rushing plays would leave Edwards facing a dangerous pressure defense.

breakdown.bottom_line: North Carolina has a path if it limits explosive plays, wins the turnover battle and protects long possessions. Miami can take control much more simply: establish early-down balance, keep Mensah comfortable and make UNC answer an offense averaging seven touchdowns' worth of points every Saturday. The first few third-down series should reveal whether this can stay competitive.
